name: Atadage Maha Walawwa ( Manor House)
description: Atadage Maha Walawwa, located in Galle, is a significant historical house that reflects the architectural and cultural heritage of Sri Lanka. Built in the early 19th century, the manor house was originally owned by a wealthy merchant family. The structure showcases a blend of European and local architectural styles, with intricate carvings and unique design elements that highlight the fusion of cultures during the colonial era. Visitors can explore the well-preserved rooms, learn about the lives of the inhabitants, and admire the stunning views of the surrounding landscape from the verandas. The property also includes a beautifully landscaped garden, which provides a serene atmosphere for reflection and enjoyment. Guided tours are available, offering deeper insights into the history and cultural significance of the site. Atadage Maha Walawwa is a must-visit for those interested in exploring Sri Lanka’s rich cultural heritage and understanding its historical context.
monsoon_note: Best to visit during dry season

name: Athapattu Walawwa (Manor House)
description: Athapattu Walawwa is a stunning example of colonial-era architecture in Sri Lanka, located in the picturesque town of Galle. The manor house was built in the early 19th century by a prominent local family and showcases the blending of European and Asian architectural styles. Visitors can explore the well-preserved rooms, which include ornate woodwork, period furniture, and intricate plaster work. The property also features a beautifully landscaped garden that provides a tranquil setting for reflection. Guided tours offer insight into the lives of the original inhabitants and the rich cultural history of the area. Athapattu Walawwa is a must-visit for those interested in Sri Lanka’s colonial past and its unique architectural heritage.
